newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT says line count sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT says line count sharply up.

text.p: Czech fixed-line telephone monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. said on Monday that lines installed rose to 27.25 percent of the population by the end of 1996 from 23.22 percent at the end of the previous year.

SPT, managed by a Dutch-Swiss consortium which is under pressure to fulfil a government contract to nearly double lines installed by 2000, said last year it had installed 417,000 new lines, surpassing its own 1996 goal of 402,000 new lines.
"We now operate 2.8 million total lines," SPT said in a statement.
It said that the proportion of digitalisation of SPT's entire network had grown to 33 percent by the end of 1996, from 18 percent at the end of 1995.
The company did not say in the statement what its goal for development of the network would be in 1997.

A consortium combining Royal PTT Netherlands and the Swiss state operator Swiss Telecom won a 27 percent stake in SPT in 1995 for $1.32 billion in cash, and promising to manage the expansion of the Czech phone network to over four million lines by the end of the century.

They have also promised to make substantial upgrades in the quality of the system through a massive programme of digitalisation of switching stations and installation of fibre-optic and better copper cable.
